# M0-c-04 — closing check of the session's hardening round S5 (lane `check/M0-c-04-close-s5`, flow-7, stage group S, 2026-11-06 – 2026-11-10)

**Verdict: PASS.** Both lines of the round (J670: Q122's S5 class, the growth stage's share; Q88's growth part) are
confirmed with this lane's own evidence. The gates pass. The refusal census of the item's registered family (M0-e-06's
site spike, every seed reaching S5) did not rise in any class of any configuration: 137 before, 125 after. RELATED@1000
has seven reds, exactly the four DECLARED and three FOREIGN of J710. This lane's new findings are notes rows N-47 – N-52
in `checks/M0-c-04-notes.md`; none is a blocker under the closing rule. Three of them are for the session now, not for
M4: N-50 (the `E_DEGENERATE` class is raised by the wall **strips**, not by the trace's re-offset rung as the builder's
rows 39 / 41 and C-0454 say — the report to M0-c-02 S6 names the right seeds and message but the wrong place), N-51
(relief-60 coarse 29 committed before the round and refuses now) and N-48 (an unwalled stage's boundary does not hold
the wall before it).

The lane is an implementer-side independent closing checker (J162) and wrote no part of the item. Its ledger row is
L-0713 in `CLEAN-ROOM.md`. Machine `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz:4cpu:16gib` (the brief's id), Node
v24.12.0, `tools/test_budget.py` = 1 before every vitest run. No git command was run.

### 1.2 The growth stage's share: two rules, read in the source

* `growth/boundary.ts` `squareGates` (:886): `if (ringIsSimple(next) && (!selfTouches(next) || selfTouches(ring))) ring = next;`
  — a squaring that adds a touch as the trace reads one is kept off. With the rule off, relief-3000 162 and 196 hand
  the trace a self-touching outline (the hook: `handedSelfTouch` true, the two gates 1.07 m apart on 162) and refuse
  F-WALL; with it on the handed outline is clean and S5 commits, in both configurations.
* `growth/mainRoads.ts` `heldBoundary` (:1043) and `heldEnclosure` (:1017): a walled stage whose plain boundary
  `crossesCore` the wall before it is taken again over the previous selection plus every reachable dry interior node
  inside that wall or within `wallClearance`. With the rule off, each of the nine relief-60 seeds hands the trace a
  boundary through its core (the hook: `handedCore` true, 1 – 19 points of stage 1's wall outside); with it on the
  handed boundary is clean (0 wall points outside) and S5 commits.

Every fixed seed is pinned through S5 on the tree: `held.test.ts` (relief-60 default 13, 84, 156, 162),
`held-coarse.test.ts` (coarse 88, 178, 188, 196, 197), `site.test.ts` (relief-3000 default and coarse 162, 196), the
unit in `boundary.test.ts`; each pin's red is this lane's rules-off derivation of the same seed (refused) and the
mutants of §4. Cost as measured here: NEAR over `s5ab/` 3 226 s at one worker (the builder names 4 453 s and 19
derivations). API frozen (J263 Q1): `heldEnclosure` and `heldBoundary` are module-private (`function`, no `export`);

reading; that the index did not change is PLAUSIBLE, there being no before image).

### 1.3 Attribution of every remaining refusal

The census copy reports the outline `traceStage` hands the trace (after `insertOnOutline` and `squareGates`). On all
124 remaining refusals that reach the trace it is simple, touches nowhere at the attraction distance, does not cross
the previous wall and leaves 0 of its points outside (`python3 probe/p4.py`: DIRTY 0). So no growth-stage boundary
defect remains in them. By message:

| message (verbatim) | seeds | raised by | owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F-WALL: the trace touches itself after the re-offset and union-simplify rungs; the later rungs are M1's (§5.2; C-0085)` (`E_SELF_INTERSECT`) | relief-60 default 38, coarse 37, relief-3000 default 18, coarse 19 (the lists of notes row 41, equal to this census seed for seed) | `enceinte/trace.ts` :202 | the wall's, REPORTED |
| `(wall, enceinte:2) branches: a linear role forms simple chains or rings (§3.10 role consistency)` (`E_INVARIANT`) | relief-60 118 (both); relief-3000 32, 81, 188 (both) | the kernel's role check on the trace's own batch (role `wall`) | the wall's, REPORTED |
| `empty` (`E_DEGENERATE`) | relief-3000 21, 59 (both) | **`enceinte/strips.ts` :642, `layStrips`' `insertChain` of a free piece** — see below | the wall strips', REPORTED, **the builder's mechanism corrected (N-50)** |
| `S5a: the gate vertices could not be put on their ways: S5a: the stage boundary crosses bridge:24's span at (25597, 119863) with 0 of its deck ends on …` (`E_INVARIANT`) | relief-60 coarse 151 | `growth/boundary.ts` `placeGateVertices` (the item's) | the item's REFUSE, `notBuilt('M3a')` |

**The `E_DEGENERATE` class (own probe, executed).** Notes rows 39 and 41 and C-0454 say that on 21 and 59 "the pull
folds … and the re-offset rung then leaves nothing (`E_DEGENERATE 'empty'`, the rung's code, `rungs.ts`)". The code
does not do that: `trace.ts` :181 – 202 turns a rung's `empty` into the rung's `why` and ends in the F-WALL
`E_SELF_INTERSECT` message, never in `E_DEGENERATE`. A stack probe on relief-3000 default 21 and 59 (every creation
of an `E_DEGENERATE` `empty` result recorded) shows the stage-2 trace **commits**, and the refusal is then raised in
the strips' batch: `layStrips` (`enceinte/strips.ts` :642) inserts a free piece of a way corridor's ring — 2 points,
28 cm on seed 21, at (−43701, 80716), beside the gate pair 14.04 m apart; 3 points, 30 cm on seed 59 — which passes
`layStrips`' own floor (`chainLength ≥ LATTICE.attractCm`, 26 cm) and which the kernel's insertion lands on existing
vertices and refuses `empty`. The raiser, the chain and the floor are all in `enceinte/strips.ts` (M0-c-02's); the
growth stage's part is only that it calls `layStrips` with a stop per gate (`stageStops`, C-0292). So the class is
the wall's as the builder reported, with the same seeds and message, but it is the **strips'**, not the trace's
rungs. The two coarse seeds carry the same message and gate gaps and were not probed (PLAUSIBLE for coarse).

**relief-60 coarse 151** stays the item's REFUSE: success needs the trace beneath a deck (`M0.md` §4b: "the raised
ways and their arena parts | M3a | … `notBuilt('M3a')`"; C-0454 (3)); the text is pinned verbatim by `span.test.ts`
"a finger of the boundary across the span with neither deck end inside is refused, named verbatim, nothing written"
(mutant M10 killed).

Not re-measured here: the builder's split of the F-WALL seeds into W1 (the water splice) and W2 (the pull) rests on its
own dump inside the trace, lost with its scratch. Given N-50, M0-c-02 S6 should take the seeds and messages from row 41
and re-derive the mechanism rather than trust the W1 / W2 labels.

the wall before it. That is not so: on all nine held seeds the unwalled stage 3 crosses stage 2's wall (the census
hook), so the mutant changes stage 3's boundary there and the pins, which assert only that S5 commits and that every
*walled* stage holds the wall before it, do not see it. The mutant is not equivalent. It is not a blocker either: the
sentence it breaks ("an unwalled stage … reads the selection") keeps the pre-round behaviour of unwalled stages, which
the round did not change — with both rules off, stage 3's plain boundary leaves 19 points of stage 2's wall outside on

their pins (M3a, M3b, M4, M5, M7). The missing pin is a further hardening test (N-47), and the behaviour it would pin
is itself a question for the session (N-48). Limit: M6 was run against `growth.test.ts`, `held.test.ts` and
`held-coarse.test.ts`, not against all of NEAR and RELATED.
